outcome: The problem as worded remains open in general (no source found settles the order of ex(n,K_{t,t}) for t of 4 or more, or the exact value of z(m,n;s,t) in general), but since 26 January 2024 exact values or new bounds have been posted for finitely many cells of z(m,n;s,t), mostly with s=t=3, plus one finite K_{2,2} cell (z(43;2) <= 294); a May 2026 preprint credits an LLM-guided evolutionary search (OpenEvolve) with three exact values and 41 lower bounds, and several second-order and hypergraph papers in the same family appeared that do not bear on the classical function.
problem_asks: (1) The Zarankiewicz function z(m,n;s,t): for bipartite graphs with parts of sizes m and n containing no complete bipartite K_{s,t}, the maximum number of edges. The statement asks how many edges such a graph can have, so the value of this function (a formula, or exact values at given parameters) is what is asked. (2) For fixed s and t, how z(n,n;s,t) grows as the number of vertices n grows: its order of magnitude (the Wikipedia article states the conjectured order Theta(n^{2-1/s}) for constant s <= t, and says the general answer is still unknown). In the diagonal case K_{t,t} this is the exponent of ex(n,K_{t,t}). (3) The unbalanced case, where the part sizes m and n vary independently (asymptotic order or exact values across the range of m against n). (4) All values of s and t, since the statement says 'a complete bipartite subgraph of a given size', not only s = t. Not asked by the bullet and recorded below only as analogues: hypergraph, induced, geometric, VC-dimension-bounded, degree-bounded, and second-order biquadratic variants.

events.what_happened: Kovari, Sos and Turan prove the double-counting upper bound z(n;t) = O(n^{2-1/t}) for K_{t,t}-free bipartite graphs; Hylten-Cavallius (1958) observes that the same argument gives the bound for z(m,n;s,t). Recorded as the baseline from which the problem starts. Read via the Wikipedia article only (opened); the original paper was not read.
events.delivers: An upper bound z(m,n;s,t) = O(n^{2-1/s}) for fixed s and t, valid for all s and t. Upper bound only.
events.remains: Every lower bound matching it, the exact values, and the unbalanced ranges.
events.direction: Upper bound that approaches the conjectured order from above; does not settle it.

events.what_happened: Reiman (1958) gives a sharp upper bound for z(n;2), matched by incidence graphs of projective planes, so that z(n;2) = (1/2 + o(1)) n^{3/2} (as stated in the Wikipedia article, opened). Background event; original papers not read.
events.delivers: The asymptotic order and leading constant of z(n;2) = z(n,n;2,2): the diagonal K_{2,2} case is settled asymptotically. Exact z(n;2) for general n is not given.
events.remains: Exact values for general n; the diagonal cases s = t >= 3; the unbalanced ranges.
events.direction: Settles the K_{2,2} asymptotic from both sides; cuts in the conjectured direction.
events.object: Incidence graphs of finite projective planes: explicit algebraic constructions achieving about n^{3/2}/2 edges with no K_{2,2} (no two points on two common lines).

events.what_happened: Brown constructs K_{3,3}-free graphs with Omega(n^{5/3}) edges from point-sphere incidences in finite affine space (Wikipedia, opened; original not read). Combined with the Kovari-Sos-Turan upper bound this gives the order of z(n;3) = Theta(n^{5/3}).
events.delivers: The order of magnitude of z(n;3) = z(n,n;3,3) (the diagonal K_{3,3} case), Theta(n^{5/3}), i.e. the conjectured order for s = t = 3 is established.
events.remains: Exact values for general n; the diagonal K_{t,t} for t >= 4; the unbalanced ranges.
events.direction: Matches the upper bound; the K_{3,3} order is settled in the direction the conjecture points.
events.object: A K_{3,3}-free bipartite graph with Omega(n^{5/3}) edges built from point-sphere incidences in a finite affine space; explicit algebraic construction.

events.what_happened: Kollar, Ronyai and Szabo (1996) give norm graphs, and Alon, Ronyai and Szabo (1999) projective norm graphs, showing ex(n,K_{s,t}) = Omega(n^{2-1/s}) when t > (s-1)! (Wikipedia, opened; originals not read).
events.delivers: The conjectured order Theta(n^{2-1/s}) for K_{s,t} whenever t > (s-1)!. For diagonal K_{t,t} this covers t = 3 only (since t > (t-1)! fails for t >= 4).
events.remains: K_{s,t} with t <= (s-1)!, including the diagonal K_{t,t} for t >= 4.
events.direction: Matches the upper bound for the stated (s,t) range; does not settle the rest.
events.object: Norm graphs over finite fields: explicit K_{s,(s-1)!+1}-free graphs with Omega(n^{2-1/s}) edges.

events.what_happened: Furedi (1996) gives z(n,n;2,t+1) = (t^{1/2} + o(1)) n^{3/2} (Wikipedia, opened; original not read).
events.delivers: Asymptotic order and constant of z(n,n;2,t+1) for every t, i.e. the s = 2 family is settled asymptotically.
events.remains: All s >= 3 with t >= s; exact values; the unbalanced ranges beyond the s = 2 family.
events.direction: Settles the s = 2 family in the direction the conjecture points.

events.what_happened: Balbuena, Garcia-Vazquez, Marcote and Valenzuela, 'Extremal K_{s,t}-free bipartite graphs', DMTCS 10(3) (2008). The abstract (opened) says new exact values of z(m,n;s,t) are obtained under parameter conditions and the extremal graphs are characterised. A search snippet attributes to it the exact value of z(m,n;t,t) for 2t <= n <= 3t-1; that sentence was not found in the abstract page read.
events.delivers: Exact values of z(m,n;s,t) under parameter conditions stated in the paper; the abstract does not give the conditions. Per a snippet only: exact z(m,n;t,t) for 2t <= n <= 3t-1 (unconfirmed).
events.remains: Everything outside the stated conditions, including most cells with m and n large relative to t.
events.doubts: The 2t <= n <= 3t-1 range comes from a search snippet, not from the page read.
events.direction: Exact values at parameter-restricted cells; does not move the general order.

events.what_happened: Collins, Riasanovsky, Wallace and Radziszowski, 'Zarankiewicz Numbers and Bipartite Ramsey Numbers' (arXiv 1604.01257, April 2016; published Journal of Algorithms and Computation 47 (2016) 63-78 per a search snippet). A computational method giving new values and upper bounds for z(m,n;s,t), 3 <= s <= 6, with a table of finite upper bounds. The table itself was not read; the values below are as quoted by 2026 preprints.
events.delivers: Finite upper bounds used as the reference table for s = t = 3, e.g. z(13,17;3,3) <= 110 and z(16,17;3,3) <= 133 as quoted by later preprints; also several exact values for other s, t.
events.remains: Those cells remain open for lower bounds in several cases; the general problem is untouched.
events.time_since_posted: not applicable (2016; journal publication per snippet)

machine_checked.system: The authors' computational method (software not read)

events.directly_checkable: Upper bounds are certified by the authors' computation; the table was not read.
events.doubts: Figures quoted by later preprints were not checked against the 2016 table.
events.direction: Upper bounds at finite cells; cuts downward on z at those cells; the general problem is not affected.

events.what_happened: Bukh, 'Random algebraic construction of extremal graphs' (arXiv 1409.3856; v1 12 Sep 2014, latest v5 23 Jul 2015; journal Bull. LMS 47 (2015) per a later reference list). The abstract (opened) calls it an expository paper presenting a motivated construction of large graphs without a given complete bipartite subgraph.
events.delivers: An expository account of the random algebraic method for K_{s,t}-free graphs. The abstract states no new bound.
events.remains: Everything, as far as the abstract shows.
events.direction: Method exposition; no direction on the problem stated in the abstract.

events.what_happened: Sudakov and Tomon, 'Turan number of bipartite graphs with no K_{t,t}' (arXiv 1910.11048, v1 24 Oct 2019; published Proc. AMS 2020 per a search snippet). Abstract (opened): for a bipartite H with one side's vertices all of degree at most t and H containing no K_{t,t}, ex(n,H) = o(n^{2-1/t}); this verifies a conjecture of Conlon, Janzer and Lee. The abstract also notes the Kovari-Sos-Turan bound is known to be sharp when s > (t-1)!.
events.delivers: A different question: the extremal number of a degree-bounded bipartite H with no K_{t,t}, not ex(n,K_{t,t}) itself. It shows the K_{t,t}-free host bound is o(n^{2-1/t}) for those H.
events.remains: ex(n,K_{t,t}) itself is not addressed.
events.direction: Analogue for a different H; does not move the K_{t,t} order.

events.what_happened: Bukh, 'Extremal graphs without exponentially-small bicliques' (arXiv 2107.04167; v1 9 Jul 2021, latest v3 6 Aug 2023). Abstract (opened): constructs K_{s,t}-free graphs for t = C^s with Omega(n^{2-1/s}) edges, matching Kovari-Sos-Turan. The Wikipedia article cites it as 'Bukh (2021, arXiv)'. A search snippet says a 2024 Duke publication; not verified.
events.delivers: The conjectured order Theta(n^{2-1/s}) for K_{s,t} with t >= C^s (C absolute constant): settles the order when t is exponentially large in s. The diagonal K_{t,t} is not covered, since it would need t >= C^t.
events.remains: Ranges s <= t < C^s, including every diagonal K_{t,t}.
events.direction: Settles the order in the regime t >= C^s; cuts in the conjectured direction there.
events.object: Explicit K_{s,t}-free graphs for t = C^s with Omega(n^{2-1/s}) edges, from a random algebraic construction (non-constructive probabilistic choice inside an algebraic family, per the method).

events.what_happened: Conlon, 'Some remarks on the Zarankiewicz problem' (arXiv 2007.12816; v1 25 Jul 2020, v3 11 Apr 2021; published Math. Proc. Camb. Phil. Soc. 2022 per snippet, DOI 10.1017/S0305004121000475). Abstract (opened): the Kovari-Sos-Turan upper bound is tight up to the constant for a broad range of parameters, via a new quantitative variant of the random algebraic method.
events.delivers: Tightness up to the constant of the upper bound for z(m,n;s,t) over a broad range of (unbalanced) parameters. The exact theorem range was not confirmed from the abstract page (a snippet is garbled).
events.remains: Parameters outside the stated range; the diagonal K_{t,t} with t >= 4 in general.

checked_by.who: Mathematical Proceedings of the Cambridge Philosophical Society (journal of record)

events.direction: Matches the upper bound over a broad range (unbalanced); cuts in the conjectured direction there.

events.what_happened: Janzer and Pohoata, 'On the Zarankiewicz problem for graphs with bounded VC-dimension' (arXiv 2009.00130; v1 31 Aug 2020, v2 2 Apr 2021). Abstract (opened): for K_{k,k}-free bipartite graphs with VC-dimension at most d, the maximum is o(n^{2-1/d}) for every k >= d >= 3 (Fox et al. had O(n^{2-1/d}), sharp only for k = d = 2). Published Combinatorica 2024 (DOI 10.1007/s00493-024-00095-2) per OpenAlex snippet.
events.delivers: A different hypothesis: the extra assumption of bounded VC-dimension d. Under it, the K_{k,k}-free maximum is o(n^{2-1/d}) for k >= d >= 3. Does not address the general K_{k,k} problem.
events.remains: The general K_{k,k} problem without the VC-dimension hypothesis.

checked_by.what_they_did: published the paper (2024-05-14 per OpenAlex snippet)

events.direction: Analogue under an added hypothesis; does not move the unrestricted problem.

events.what_happened: Conlon, Mattheus, Mubayi and Verstraete, 'Ramsey numbers and the Zarankiewicz problem' (arXiv 2307.08694, July 2023; v2 April 2024; Bull. LMS 56 (2024) 2014-2023 per a VUB portal snippet). Links bipartite Ramsey-type numbers r(F,t) to a 0-1 matrix Zarankiewicz variant that forbids a finite family of submatrices; gives lower bounds for cycle-complete Ramsey numbers. Not opened; from search snippets only.
events.revisions: v2 April 2024 (snippet); the first public written argument is the July 2023 posting.
events.delivers: A matrix-family variant of the Zarankiewicz function, used for Ramsey numbers. Not the classical z(m,n;s,t). Includes a conditional result on a Zarankiewicz conjecture (not read).
events.remains: The classical problem.

checked_by.who: Bulletin of the London Mathematical Society (journal of record)
checked_by.what_they_did: published the paper (2024, per VUB portal snippet)

events.direction: Analogue (matrix-family variant); no direction on the classical problem.

events.what_happened: Hunter, Milojevic, Sudakov and Tomon, 'Kovari-Sos-Turan theorem for hereditary families' (arXiv 2401.10853; v1 19 Jan 2024, v2 29 Apr 2025; J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 172 (2025) 168-197, per the arXiv page). Abstract (opened): conjectures that an induced H-free and K_{s,s}-free graph has at most a modest number of extra edges compared with an H-free graph, with supporting cases (trees, cycles, the cube, bounded-degree bipartite H).
events.delivers: A different question: induced-H-free plus K_{s,s}-free hosts. Its K_{s,s} hypothesis is the classical one, but the object counted is different; it does not bound z(m,n;s,t).
events.remains: The classical z(m,n;s,t).

checked_by.who: Journal of Combinatorial Theory Series B (journal of record)

events.direction: Analogue: induced-H question; no direction on the classical function.

events.what_happened: Chen, Horsley and Mammoliti, 'Exact values for unbalanced Zarankiewicz numbers' (arXiv 2202.05507, 2022; J. Graph Theory, doi 10.1002/jgt.23068). Per search snippets: for s = 2 and large m, Z_{2,t}(m,n) determined exactly in almost all remaining cases (n of order t m^2), plus new upper bounds. Not opened; snippet only.
events.revisions: Journal version (J. Graph Theory) year not confirmed.
events.delivers: Exact values of z(m,n;2,t) for large m in almost all remaining unbalanced cases (s = 2 only), and new families of upper bounds. Per snippet.
events.remains: s >= 3; the balanced and diagonal cases; the cases where the floor of the bound is not attained.

checked_by.who: Journal of Graph Theory (journal of record)

events.direction: Exact values in the s = 2 unbalanced family; cuts in the direction of the known bounds, not the conjectured order.

events.what_happened: Davies, Gill and Horsley, 'Improved upper bounds on Zarankiewicz numbers' (arXiv 2411.18842; v1 28 Nov 2024, v2 13 Dec 2025). They add constraints to Roman's linear-programming bound for z(m,n;s,t), giving new upper bounds for many small parameter sets, and a closed-form family of upper bounds generalising Chen-Horsley-Mammoliti (who treated s = 2). Journal: Discrete Math. 349 (2026) 114924 (DOI 10.1016/j.disc.2025.114924), per the arXiv page. Full text (v2 HTML) read.
events.delivers: New upper bounds on z(m,n;s,t) at many finite parameter sets, including a table for s = t = 3 (per search snippet; table not read). A closed-form family of upper bounds for general s, which the abstract says generalises the s = 2 result of Chen-Horsley-Mammoliti. No lower bounds, no change to the asymptotic order.
events.remains: Lower bounds at the cells where the bound is not attained; exact values beyond those; asymptotic order for any s and t.

checked_by.who: Discrete Mathematics (journal of record), its referees and editors
checked_by.qualification: peer-reviewed journal acceptance of a combinatorics paper by three combinatorialists (Horsley is an established extremal graph theorist)
checked_by.what_they_did: accepted and published the paper (volume 349, issue 5, 2026)

events.directly_checkable: The LP constraints and the claimed bounds can be re-solved; the full text states the LP is implemented in Python with the GLPK solver via SageMath, so a rerun is possible.
events.direction: Tightens upper bounds at finite cells; cuts toward smaller z at those cells; nothing about lower bounds or the asymptotic order.

events.what_happened: Chan, Keller and Smorodinsky, 'On Zarankiewicz's Problem for Intersection Hypergraphs of Geometric Objects' (arXiv 2412.06490; v1 9 Dec 2024, v2 11 Sep 2025). Sharp bounds for r-partite intersection hypergraphs of axis-parallel boxes and pseudo-discs, and an improvement by a factor of about n^{(2r-2)/(3r-2)} for discs. A preliminary version was at SoCG 2025 (per search snippet; not opened).
events.delivers: A hypergraph analogue for geometric intersection hypergraphs: O(t n^{r-1} (log n / log log n)^{d-1}) for boxes and O(t n^{r-1} (log n)^{r-2}) for pseudo-discs. Says nothing about the bipartite K_{s,t} function.
events.remains: The classical bipartite problem (a different question).

checked_by.what_they_did: accepted a preliminary version with weaker results (per search snippet; not opened)

events.direction: Different question: hypergraph analogue with geometric structure. No direction on the classical problem.

events.what_happened: Christopher D. Rosin, 'Using Code Generation to Solve Open Instances of Combinatorial Design Problems' (arXiv 2501.17725; v1 29 Jan 2025). The CPro1 protocol uses LLMs to generate code that builds combinatorial designs, with a verifier checking candidate output. Per the paper's Table 1 'This paper' column (read from the HTML rendering, which the fetch flagged as garbled), it reports a packing array with N >= 31 for k = 5 and v = 6. Sadhu (arXiv 2608.01606, event sadhu-2026-08-08) cites this as 'Rosin [21] reached 31 again in 2025 using large-language-model code generation', so the packing-array lower bound 31 for pa(5;6) enters the z(43;2) argument.
events.delivers: A lower bound: a packing array PA(31,5,6) exists, i.e. the hexary packing number pa(5;6) >= 31. This is a packing-array question, not the Zarankiewicz function. It is an ingredient of the z(43;2) upper bound in sadhu-2026-08-08.
events.remains: The Zarankiewicz problem is not addressed. For the packing number, the exact value was addressed later by Sadhu (2026).

checked_by.qualification: author of the z(43;2) paper, which relies on pa(5;6)
checked_by.what_they_did: cites the N = 31 array as a lower bound and separately establishes the upper bound by exhaustive search; no independent re-check of Rosin's array is described

events.time_since_posted: about 20 months; cited by a 2026 paper for the value 31

machine_checked.system: verifier inside the CPro1 pipeline (described in the abstract as checking generated code output)

events.directly_checkable: A packing array PA(31,5,6) is a 31-row, 5-column array over six symbols in which every pair of columns contains each ordered pair of symbols at most once. This is checkable by brute force. The array itself was not reproduced in the text read.
events.doubts: (a) The N >= 31 entry was read from a garbled HTML table; its column placement is inferred from table structure. (b) The abstract does not state the number 31. (c) The only other 31 in the text is a development log, 'solves N=31 k=5 v=6 in 1 out of 2 attempts'. (d) Which model produced the N = 31 array is not stated in the text read.
events.direction: Raises the packing-array lower bound for k = 5, v = 6. Cuts no way on the Zarankiewicz problem.
events.object: A packing array PA(31,5,6): a 31-row, 5-column array over six symbols with every pair of columns containing each ordered pair of symbols at most once. Found by LLM-generated search code, so an explicit array rather than an existence proof. The array itself was not printed in the text read.

events.what_happened: Hunter, Milojevic, Tomon and Sudakov, 'C4-free subgraphs of high degree with geometric applications' (arXiv 2506.23942; submitted 30 Jun 2025). A graph of average degree d has either an induced C4-free subgraph of average degree at least k, or a d-vertex subgraph with Omega_k(d^2) edges; applied to many geometric Zarankiewicz-type problems. Abstract opened; body read to the truncation point in Section 3.
events.delivers: A structural dichotomy for induced C4-free subgraphs and optimal bounds for geometric Zarankiewicz-type problems. These are different questions from z(m,n;s,t).
events.remains: The classical bipartite problem.
events.time_since_posted: about 15 months; no review or journal found in the searches run, but not searched for separately
events.direction: Analogue (geometric and induced). No direction on the classical problem.

events.what_happened: Mubayi, 'Hypergraphs without complete partite subgraphs' (arXiv 2507.06390; v1 8 Jul 2025, v2 14 Jul 2025; Combinatorics, Probability and Computing 35 (2026) 290-293 per the arXiv page). For complete r-partite r-uniform hypergraphs K(s_1,...,s_{r-1},t), the Zarankiewicz number is n^{r-1/s-o(1)} (s the product of the first r-1 parts) once t > 3^{s+o(s)}, improving the factorial threshold of Pohoata and Zakharov; gives z(n,K(2,2,7)) = n^{11/4-o(1)}. Read in full (v2 HTML, no truncation note).
events.delivers: A hypergraph analogue with an exponential threshold on t. The paper's main result concerns r >= 3 hypergraphs; the r = 2 case is not addressed in what was read. It does not settle the classical bipartite problem.
events.remains: The classical bipartite problem for diagonal K_{t,t}, t >= 4, and general (s,t) for graphs.

checked_by.who: Combinatorics, Probability and Computing (journal of record)

events.direction: Hypergraph analogue; threshold improved. No direction on the classical graph problem.

events.what_happened: Gao, Hou, Huang and Wang, 'Tight bounds towards Zarankiewicz problem in hypergraph' (arXiv 2510.14869; submitted 16 Oct 2025). For ordered r-partite r-graphs, the Zarankiewicz number is Theta(m_1...m_{r-1} n^{1-1/(s_1...s_{r-1})}) over a range of parameters, extending Conlon (2022). Full text read.
events.delivers: A hypergraph analogue Theta-bound, lower bound under s <= t and m <= n^{...}, matching upper bound under further conditions (Corollary 1.4). Restricted to the hypergraph range.
events.remains: The classical bipartite problem outside the graph case; the unrestricted parameter range.
events.time_since_posted: about 12 months; no review or journal found in the searches run, but not searched for separately
events.direction: Analogue (ordered hypergraph). No direction on the classical problem.

events.what_happened: Bhan, Nobili, Langer (and Raghuraman in some listings), 'New Bounds for Zarankiewicz Numbers via Reinforced LLM Evolutionary Search' (arXiv 2605.01120; v1 1 May 2026, cs.AI primary, math.CO; later versions exist, including one listed in August 2026). The authors state: exact values Z(11,21;3,3)=116, Z(11,22;3,3)=121, Z(12,22;3,3)=132, which they call the first time these were determined; lower bounds for 41 further cells (of 44 open cells among 51 (m,n) pairs for s = t = 3); and four matched prior values. Their construction method is OpenEvolve, an LLM-driven evolutionary search whose mutations are generated by named LLMs (see ai). Full text (v1 HTML) read.
events.revisions: v1 1 May 2026; a v2 is cited by later papers (May 2026); the abstract page showed v3 at fetch time, date not confirmed.
events.delivers: Exact values of z(m,n;3,3) at three cells (11,21), (11,22), (12,22), and lower bounds at 41 further cells of the s = t = 3 table. Restricted to K_{3,3} and finitely many cells. The exactness claims are matched against upper bounds taken from prior literature (the paper names Tan and Davies et al. as its comparison, per the full-text read).
events.remains: All other (m,n) cells for s = t = 3 (44 open cells, of which 41 get only lower bounds), all other (s,t), and the asymptotic order. The authors list extending beyond the diagonal s = t = 3 and extending evolutionary discovery to proving upper bounds as future work.
events.time_since_posted: about 5 months; no independent check of the three exact values found. Later papers (Saurabh, Aug 2026) use its figure values as baseline, and Saurabh reports the same authors re-verified Saurabh's own matrices in July 2026, which is a different event.
events.directly_checkable: Each lower bound is a 0-1 matrix with no all-ones 3x3 submatrix, checkable by brute force over row triples. The paper's generated algorithms include validity checks that print violating row triples (Algorithm 5 per full-text read). Witness matrices for the three exact values were not confirmed in the text read.
events.doubts: (a) Exactness rests on upper bounds from prior literature (Tan; Davies et al.); the three exact claims are only as good as those bounds. (b) Priority: the abstract calls Z(12,22;3,3)=132 a first determination, but Afrasyab (2608.08154) lists Z(12,n;3,3)=6n for 18 <= n <= 22 and says the n = 22 equality is retained as prior material (see disputes). (c) Constructions come from generated programs; reproduction depends on those programs. (d) Preprint, not peer-reviewed. (e) Author list differs across sources.
events.direction: Exact values at three finite cells and lower bounds at 41 more, all for s = t = 3. These are determinations of the classical function at specific points, not asymptotic results. Several lower bounds lie within one edge of the best known upper bound.
events.object: Explicit 0-1 matrices avoiding an all-ones 3x3 submatrix, produced by the LLM-guided search, one per cell. The paper reports the generation algorithms and implementation. Example reported in the appendix (search snippet only): an 8x23 matrix with 94 ones. The witnesses for the exact values were not confirmed in the text read.

systems.name: OpenEvolve
systems.what_it_did: The evolutionary framework that produced the constructions: an LLM-driven loop that iteratively improves generated programs, with a reward the authors tailored to this problem. The constructions and generation algorithms reported are its output.
systems.basis_quote: Our results are obtained using OpenEvolve, an open-source evolutionary algorithm based on Large Language Models (LLMs) that iteratively improves algorithms for generating mathematical constructions by optimizing a reward signal which we tailored for this specific problem.

events.what_happened: Lofberg and Qi, 'Second Order Zarankiewicz Number' (arXiv 2608.30555; posted August 2026, exact day not read; v3 manuscript dated 13 Sep 2026). Introduces or studies the second-order number z_2(m,n) for irreducible doubly simple biquadratic forms, with intermediate parameters z_RL and z_SL. Reported results (per the full-text read, first 100,000 characters of about 128,600): z_2(5,4)=z_SL(5,4)=z_RL(5,4)=13 vs z_wL=12; z_2(6,4)=16; z_2(m,3)=2m for m >= 3; a cubic separation along an incidence family; z_SL(15,6)=z_2(15,6)=60; conjecture z_2 = z_RL. Analogue, not the classical function.

disputes.summary: Bhan, Nobili and Langer state that Z(11,21;3,3)=116, Z(11,22;3,3)=121 and Z(12,22;3,3)=132 are the first determinations of these exact values. Afrasyab's Theorem 1.1 lists Z(12,n;3,3)=6n for 18 <= n <= 22 and says the n = 22 equality is 'retained as prior material rather than claimed as new'. Who first established Z(12,22;3,3)=132, and when, is not established by the text read; the Collins et al. and Davies et al. upper-bound tables are the likely prior sources but were not checked cell by cell.

summary: The problem as worded is open: no source found settles the order of ex(n,K_{t,t}) for t >= 4 or gives z(m,n;s,t) in general, and every source read (Wikipedia, revised 25 Oct 2025; the Smorodinsky survey of 24 Sep 2024; Bhan et al. May 2026) still describes it as open. Settled cases are old: K_{2,2} asymptotically (Reiman 1958 with projective planes; Furedi 1996 for all t), K_{3,3} (Brown 1966 with Kovari-Sos-Turan), K_{s,t} for t > (s-1)! (norm graphs, Kollar-Ronyai-Szabo 1996, Alon-Ronyai-Szabo 1999), and K_{s,t} for t >= C^s (Bukh 2021). Since 26 January 2024 the classical function has moved only at finitely many cells, all listed as events above: Davies, Gill and Horsley (Nov 2024) gave new upper bounds via linear-programming constraints; Bhan, Nobili and Langer (1 May 2026) gave exact values at three s = t = 3 cells and lower bounds at 41 more, using OpenEvolve with named LLMs; Hou (9 Aug 2026) gave seven exact s = t = 3 values from one 13x18 matrix, with no AI named; Afrasyab (8 Aug 2026) gave exact values that agree with Hou's on five overlapping cells and extend them to z(13,22;3,3)=137, disclosing 'OpenAI GPT 5.6 Sol High' for 'exploratory reasoning, implementation, verification, manuscript integration, and packaging'; Saurabh (27 Aug 2026) gave five lower bounds by a classical search run by an autonomous system named NOVA, whose text says it uses no language model; Sadhu (8 Aug 2026) gave z(43;2) <= 294 for one K_{2,2} cell, using pa(5;6) = 31, whose lower bound 31 Sadhu credits to Rosin (29 Jan 2025), a CPro1 LLM-code-generation result for packing arrays. Several in-window papers in the same family are analogues and are recorded but not counted as bearing on the classical function: the second-order biquadratic papers of Lofberg, Qi and coauthors (Aug-Sep 2026), the hypergraph and geometric variants (Chan-Keller-Smorodinsky; Mubayi; Gao-Hou-Huang-Wang; Hunter-Milojevic-Tomon-Sudakov). Close calls: (1) whether exact values at single cells, e.g. z(11,21;3,3)=116, move 'the problem' or only a case of it, which the record leaves to the judging pass, with the direction and remains fields written for each; (2) whether Afrasyab's AI statement is load-bearing, since the quote names 'implementation' and 'exploratory reasoning' but not the mathematical content, and the author says sole responsibility for the mathematics; (3) whether NOVA is an AI system, which the paper answers only by saying the search is classical; (4) whether Rosin's packing-array result counts, since it is not the Zarankiewicz function and enters only as an ingredient of the z(43;2) bound; (5) whether Bhan et al.'s exact values are as secure as their witnesses, since their exactness rests on upper bounds from Tan and Davies et al., and the priority claim for Z(12,22;3,3)=132 is contested (see disputes); (6) whether Hou's and Afrasyab's agreement on five cells is independent confirmation, given that both are single-author preprints with no peer review, and that Hou's (12,18) value and Afrasyab's 12-row family both rely on computer enumeration. The AI search covered: the problem name with LLM, AlphaEvolve, FunSearch, OpenEvolve, GPT, Claude, Gemini and Erdos-problem terms; Terence Tao's blog and Mastodon (no Zarankiewicz AI post found, only Erdos-problem posts); Quanta (no article found). The AI-credit lead in Lofberg and Qi (2608.30555), which a search snippet describes as an OpenAI model used for proof exploration, hypothesis generation and proof-verification code, could not be confirmed because the acknowledgements were not reached in the text fetched, so it is not recorded as a system.
competing_reading: Read strictly, nothing in the window moved the problem: every in-window result is a finite cell of z(m,n;s,t), a finite K_{2,2} cell, a packing-array number or an analogue, and the problem asks for the function's general order and exact formula. On that reading every event is a case, and the status of the problem is unchanged. Read loosely, the exact values of Bhan et al., Hou and Afrasyab are determinations of the classical function at specific points, which the problem's wording ('how many edges can there be ... given number of vertices') covers. For AI: a reader who treats OpenEvolve as a computational tool rather than an AI system would drop Bhan et al. from the AI count, though the authors say 'LLM-guided' throughout and name Gemini 2.0 Flash and Claude models. Afrasyab's disclosure could be read as only proofreading and typesetting, since 'implementation' may mean typing up a result the author already had.
what_would_settle_it: (a) The full PDF or HTML of arXiv 2608.30555 (Lofberg and Qi), acknowledgements section, to confirm or drop the OpenAI-model lead. (b) Bhan et al.'s appendix witnesses and the tables behind their Figure 2 and their exactness claim, and the Tan and Davies et al. bounds they cite, to confirm the three exact values from the constructions plus those bounds. (c) Whether Z(12,22;3,3)=132 appears in Collins et al. (2016) or Davies et al. (2024) as an upper bound matched by a known construction, to settle the priority dispute. (d) Afrasyab's replay script and Hou's supplementary verifier, run against the 13x18 and 13x22 claims. (e) An explicit statement from Saurabh or the NOVA authors on whether NOVA uses any learned or language-model component. (f) The Rosin (2501.17725) experiment section for which model produced PA(31,5,6), and the Table 1 entry read directly from a PDF. (g) Peer-review or journal records for the 2026 preprints, which would convert the concurrence between Hou and Afrasyab into review. (h) The v1 dates of 2608.30555, 2608.01606 and 2609.25974, which were not read.
